findings.label: L1
findings.text:
`tests/test_memory_sync_characterization.py:98` GIT_NOISE regex `(error|hint|To) ` (used with `.match`) has no colon, so it does not drop git's `error: ` / `hint: ` lines as the docstring (:63-66) says. It drops only lines starting `To ` or `error `/`hint ` with no colon. Evidence: `goldens/sync/validator.txt:455` keeps `error: failed to push some refs to '<TMP>/remote.git'`.
Effect: this hides nothing, because it erases less than documented. But the golden now carries git's own wording, which depends on the git version and so can go red on a different git for no reason of ours. The docstring is also wrong about the rule. Fix one or the other.

findings.label: L2
findings.text: `skills/ai-task/memory_hook.py:12` The section header "status, show" sits over `hook_state`, which is hook code. `memory_status.py` has no header at all, and `memory_hook.py:32` then opens "the git hook". Cosmetic and misleading.

findings.label: L3
findings.text: `tests/fixtures/state/partition.json:280,354` `lazy` of `memory_modules` (`["memory_store","memory_sync"]`) and of `memory_after_close` (`["memory_sync"]`) now name a module that neither imports. Nothing reads `lazy` (`grep lazy tests/test_state_layout.py` is empty), so the false data is inert today, but a later WP that reads it will be misled. The plan accepted this. Deviation 4a (the 16 `signature` renames `sync`→`mem`) is correct and forced: `test_state_layout.py:167` compares those signatures against the code through `ast`, and it adds no behavioural expectation. I judge it acceptable under R6, but it should be recorded as a deliberate R6 exception.

findings.label: I1
findings.text: `tests/test_memory_sync_characterization.py` LINE_ORDER (sorts .jsonl record lines) and BYTES (`N bytes`) are the only erasures that go beyond the plan's list. I judge neither hides a moved SELF, a changed file or a changed order a user sees. LINE_ORDER touches only the on-disk listing hash; stdout order (`show`, `export`, `verify`) is still pinned verbatim, and a package's header line stays first. BYTES hides only the printed size; the file content is still pinned by the listing hash. The docstring says "Nothing else is erased", and the docstring and `RULES` are kept consistent by `test_docstring_lists_every_rule`.

findings.label: I2
findings.text: `skills/ai-task/rr_state/memory_cmd.py:24-45` An install missing any of the ten modules dies with the same text but names whichever import fails first. The plan accepted this.

findings.label: I3
findings.text: The two residuals the plan said stay (export skips keys that already have a seal; `memory enable` through a dialog pick leaves no committed record) are untouched and pinned by the golden. They are not new bugs.
